newsitem.title: USA: Pilot who saved plane says too busy to be scared.
newsitem.headline: Pilot who saved plane says too busy to be scared.

text.p: An Air Force pilot who glided his engine-dead F-16 fighter plane to a safe landing last year insisted on Tuesday he had no time to be terrified because his head was too full of glide calculations.

"The things that were really going through my head (were) my altitude and my distance from the airport," Capt. Chris Rose said at a Pentagon news conference. "I was just constantly doing math. Can I make it?"

Rose's successful landing at Elizabeth, North Carolina, last June 26 was shown on television networks that night. This week he was awarded the Air Force Kolligan Trophy that goes to the pilot who most successfully copes with an emergency.
"Capt. Rose's outstanding airmanship skills and calm demeanor saved a $20 million aircraft and perhaps many lives," Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ronald Fogleman said in a statement.
Rose landed the plane on a short 7,000-foot (2133 metre) runway after the engine of his F-16 flamed out 15 miles (24 km) away and 13,000 feet (3,962 metres) in the air, above clouds.

He told reporters that he was in position to eject from the plane all the way down but had practiced gliding the plane in routine training and knew from a pre-flight briefing that the landing strip was there in case of an emergency.

When he came out of the clouds, he said, he had to make a right turn to line up with the runway and had to make up for the lack of engine power by approaching the landing strip steeper and landing faster than normal, nearly 200 miles an hour (322 kmph) compared to a normal 130 miles an hour (209 kmph).
A cockpit videotape of the glide recorded Rose talking calmly to ground controllers through the glide and telling them after landing, "No problem. Thanks for your help."
He said he did not worry any time during the glide that he might have to ditch a $20 million plane.
"Not at the time," he said. "I think about that every day but not at the time."
